reasoning: The package is a straightforward AIMP skin theme that downloads from the official AIMP website (aimp.ru) with a pinned SHA256 checksum. The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments and a package() function that performs routine file operations (extraction with bsdtar, file copying, permission setting). No code injection, no execution of fetched content, no network requests to unrelated hosts. Report 2 (deepseek) successfully reviewed both files and correctly identified this as safe. Reports 1 and 3 were inconclusive due to tool errors (API failure and parsing failure respectively), not security concerns. Report 3 is advisory-only and doesn't count as a vote.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool errors, not substantive security analysis differences. Report 1 (qwen) failed with HTTP 400 error during PKGBUILD review. Report 3 (openrouter/free) had a parsing failure when the model returned an unexpected format for .SRCINFO. Report 2 (deepseek) successfully completed review of both files. The initial PKGBUILD audit in Report 1 actually succeeded and found it safe, but the formal review step failed.
coverage_issues: Report 1 (qwen): API error (HTTP 400) prevented formal PKGBUILD review, though initial audit succeeded
Report 3 (openrouter/free): Model returned non-standard format for .SRCINFO review, causing parsing failure
learnings: Implement retry logic for transient API errors (HTTP 400/500) to prevent inconclusive verdicts from tool failures
Add robust parsing fallbacks for model responses that don't match expected XML/JSON format - extract decision from partial responses when possible
Distinguish between 'initial audit succeeded but formal review failed' vs 'complete failure' in error reporting to provide better context for adjudication
Consider the package type (theme/skin packages with only metadata and simple file operations) when assessing risk - these have minimal attack surface
